## Part 1. Multiple Choice Questions (Select all answers that apply)

**1) According to the Illinois pension article, using a higher assumed discount rate will:** (3 marks)

<u>a. Increase reported pension liabilities
c. Increase required contributions today</u>

**2) Why are overly optimistic pension return assumptions problematic?** (3 marks)

a. They understate liabilities
b. They shift risk to future taxpayers

**3) According to the Nuveen/Schroders article, consolidation in asset management is primarily driven by:** (3 marks)
a. Regulatory capital requirements
b. Need for scale
c. Fee compression from passive investing
d. Declining demand for investment products

**4) What types of synergies are expected in the Nuveen–Schroders deal?** (3 marks)
a. Geographic diversification
b. Complementary distribution channels
c. Reduction in portfolio risk through diversification
d. Increased pricing power

**5) From the hedge fund weather modeling article, why are firms willing to pay large sums for meteorologists?** (3 marks)
a. Weather directly impacts commodity prices
b. Weather models create arbitrage opportunities
c. Climate volatility increases forecasting value
d. Regulation requires weather risk expertise

**6) If SpaceX is added to the S&P 500 shortly after IPO, which of the following are likely consequences?** (3 marks)
a. Immediate increase in firm profitability
b. Temporary upward pressure on tax rates
c. Index funds will purchase the stock
d. Decreased liquidity for SpaceX bonds

**7) Based on the "Bonds Are Still Safe" article, key dimensions investors must choose include:** (3 marks)
a. Duration (maturity)
b. Credit quality
c. Dividend yield
d. Currency exposure

**8) According to the Microsoft bond article, why might AAA corporate bonds trade at lower yields than Treasuries?** (3 marks)
a. Corporates are less risky than the U.S. government
b. Extremely strong demand for high-quality corporate bonds
c. Corporate bonds generally have lower fees
d. Pension funds are not allowed to buy corporate bonds due to regulatory constraints

**9) If banning dividends and buybacks leads firms to reinvest more in their core business, why might shareholders still oppose such a policy?** (3 marks)
a. Managers may allocate capital inefficiently
b. Shareholders prefer increased regulation
c. Firms may overinvest in negative NPV projects
d. Retained earnings eliminate all financial risk

**10) Which of the following best describes a socially valuable role of dividends and share repurchases?** (3 marks)
a. They allow firms to permanently increase their stock price
b. They recycle capital from mature firms to investors, who can reallocate it to higher-return opportunities elsewhere in the economy
c. They reduce firms' tax liabilities and therefore increase government revenue
d. They eliminate the need for firms to invest in long-term projects

**11) A firm is choosing between two depreciation methods for a new investment:** (3 marks)
Method A: Straight-line depreciation over 5 years (capital expenses recognized evenly)
Method B: Accelerated depreciation (more expense recognized in earlier years)
Assuming the firm is profitable and can fully utilize tax deductions, which of the following best explains why the firm might prefer Method B?
a. It increases total depreciation over the life of the asset
b. It reduces total taxes paid over the life of the asset
c. It reduces taxes earlier, increasing the present value of tax savings
d. It increases reported accounting earnings in early years

## Part 2. Short Calculation Question (please show your work to get full credit)

**12) You own the common stock of Grid Batteries. Grid will pay its first annual dividend of $3.00 one year from today. Grid's dividends are predicted to grow by 15% per annum in perpetuity. If this prediction is correct, what is the present value of the dividend stream of this company? Assume the appropriate discount rate is 20% annually.** (5 marks)

**13) I recently purchased a house for $1.4 million. As part of this transaction, I took out a mortgage from a bank where I put down a downpayment equal to 25% of the home value and borrowed the rest of the money from the bank at an interest rate of 6.375%. My expected property taxes on this property are $32,000 per year. What is my leverage ratio?** (5 marks)

**14) I have been raising money from venture capital investment firms for my start-up company, DeepDish Labs. Here is a list of the companies I have raised money from. What is the best estimate for the current post-money valuation of DeepDish Labs?** (5 marks)

Catalyst Ridge Ventures – June 2024, bought 5% of DeepDish Labs for $1.0 million
Foundry Peak Capital – December 2024, bought 3% of DeepDish Labs for $1.3 million
North Harbor Ventures – May 2025, bought 3.7% of DeepDish Labs for $2.0 million
SignalFire Partners – October 2025, bought 4% of DeepDish Labs for $2.3 million
Summit Arc Capital - March 2026, bought 5.5% of DeepDish Labs for $3.3 million

**15) An auto plant for a new line of magnetic induction autos will cost $1,400 billion to construct. Assume that the plant is available immediately. If successful, the present value of revenues will be $2,400 billion. If unsuccessful, the present value of revenues will be $800 billion. The probability of success is estimated at 35%. We will know immediately after plant completion whether the new auto line will be successful.** (10 marks)

**a. Would you agree to build the plant?** (5 marks)

**b. Would you agree to build the plant if you knew that you could sell the plant for $900 billion to another automaker immediately after you learn whether the new auto line is successful or unsuccessful?** (5 marks)
